title: Change-to-live under 10 seconds: measure the Linux dev-channel loop and cut it
goal: CEO direction 2026-11-11: Susi core under 10 s. Measure every phase of a genuine source change reaching the verified live dev-channel executable on Linux x86_64 (local-channel deliver), separately from cold and warm build times, and remove the largest avoidable costs until a root-package change goes live in under 10 s, without dropping its tests or verification.
acceptance: cargo run --offline --locked -p xtask --bin local-channel -- deliver --prove-rollback -- os capabilities --help (repeated, real commits)
host: Claude Code cloud session, Linux x86_64, 4 vCPU, 15 GiB RAM, Rust 1.99.0 (pinned)

results.safety: stale root snapshot refused: exit 1, nothing promoted, channel digest and live ref unchanged

limitations: deliver runs the owning packages' unit tests only; a change that breaks only a dependent package's tests can reach the dev channel (pre-existing, documented).
The concurrent path needs a second warm target directory: one-time 94.6 s and 2.4 GB here.

Test executables run directly, not through cargo: the run sets CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR, CARGO_PKG_NAME and the package directory as cwd, not every variable cargo sets. A test needing another runtime cargo variable fails (fails closed), it cannot falsely pass.
Measured on Linux x86_64 only; Windows timings not re-measured. The production channel still requires cargo local-release qualify.
